method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); dates in a small module, the rules in one module and the claimant's questions in a seat module importing it; one regulative rule (the time limits of ss 33(2), 39A(3), 41(8)) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.

seat: the claimant on a deceased person's estate: the individual with a claim on, or in, the estate -- the surviving spouse or partner, a child or stepchild, a dependant, a relative entitled on intestacy, a beneficiary under the will, a person who may ask to see the will, and the family member or beneficiary concerned with a claim that survives the death, including a beneficiary sued on such a claim (qsa-seat.l4)

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics were read; satisfied assertions were counted by distinct source range. Expected values worked by hand from the text.
